## Encrypting your data using Cryptomator
You can work with your data locally and offline, and synchronize data stored on Research Drive with Nextcloud.  To get started,[install Nexcloud](https://nextcloud.com/install/#desktop-files) and follow the instruction to [set up your NextCloud environment](https://servicedesk.surf.nl/wiki/spaces/WIKI/pages/117178931/RD+Getting+the+Nextcloud+desktop+app).

If you need to work offline with privacy-sensitive data, you may be required to encrypt it. An easy way to do this is to use the free tool Cryptomator.

Cryptomator is available for Windows, MacOS and Linux. 

## Using Cryptomator
Download and install [Nextcloud](https://nextcloud.com/install/#desktop-files).

You can follow the instructions to [set up your NextCloud environment](https://servicedesk.surf.nl/wiki/spaces/WIKI/pages/117178931/RD+Getting+the+Nextcloud+desktop+app).

When you set up the program it will ask you the name of the server to connect to. Here you have to use the VU RD environment url: https://vu.data.surf.nl/ 
For example: https://tst-test.data.surfsara.nl. 

## Install Cryptomator
Download and install from the [Cryptomator](https://cryptomator.org/) site.

## Create a new Cryptomator vault
1. Click on the + sign and choose “Create New Vault”

![Create Cryptomator Vault](/public/tools/researchdrive/Create-new-vault.png)

2. Give the folder a name

![Folder name](/public/tools/researchdrive/Folder-name.png)

3. Choose a location within NextCloud. Expert settings can be ignored 

![Cryptomator folder](/public/tools/researchdrive/Location-choice.png)

4. Set a passphrase

![Enter passphrase](/public/tools/researchdrive/Choose-passphrase-RK.png)

5. Make sure to create a recovery key 

![Recovery key](/public/tools/researchdrive/RK.png)

6. The vault will look like a normal folder in NextCloud

![Vault location](/public/tools/researchdrive/Folder-location.png)

7. When you doubleclick the new folder you will be asked for the passphrase. Enter the correct passphrase and the folder will be opened as normal. You can now work with the vault as with a normal folder.  

![Enter passphrase](/public/tools/researchdrive/Passphrase.png)
